title: Prove Kahan summation beats naive sequential on an ill-conditioned sum (CUDA)
info: single thread; fixture is [1e16, 1.0 x1000, -1e16] -- true sum is exactly 1000.0

this simulator's arithmetic runs at double precision (no real fp32 truncation), so the fixture uses a magnitude ratio (1e16) extreme enough to trigger the same catastrophic-cancellation failure at double precision that a naive fp32 sum shows on real hardware
